The buildup narrows the blood vessels.

Atorvastatin helps prevent this buildup.
This is done by slowing cholesterol production.
This keeps blood flowing more freely to vital organs.

Atorvastatin FDA-approved uses:
To reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in adults with:
Multiple risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), but without established CHD.
Use: to reduce the risk of myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina.
Type 2 diabetes and multiple risk factors for CHD, without established CHD Use: to help reduce the risk of MI and stroke.

It is used to reduce the risk of fatal and non-fatal stroke.
It is used to reduce the risk of revascularization procedures.
It is used to reduce the risk of hospitalization for congestive heart failure.
It is used to reduce the risk of angina.
As an adjunct to diet to lower LDL-C:
Adults with primary hyperlipidemia.
Adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
As an adjunct to other LDL-lowering therapies:
For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

It decreases the number of LDL particles.
It improves the body's ability to clear cholesterol.

Levothyroxine is a man-made form of thyroxine (T4), one of the hormones your thyroid gland normally produces.
It belongs to a class of medications called hormones.
It works by replacing thyroid hormone that your body is not making enough of.
Levothyroxine is used in adults and children, including newborn babies, to:
treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid - a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone).
It replaces the missing hormone whether the condition was present from birth or developed later.
It replaces the missing hormone whether the problem starts in the thyroid gland itself or in the pituitary gland or hypothalamus.
lower the level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood in people being treated for a certain type of thyroid cancer, alongside surgery and radioactive iodine therapy.
Levothyroxine injection is used in adults to treat myxedema coma.
Myxedema coma is a rare and life-threatening complication.
Myxedema coma is a complication of a severely underactive thyroid.
Without thyroid hormone, your body cannot function properly.

Levothyroxine is a man-made form of thyroxine (T4), one of the hormones your thyroid gland normally produces.
It belongs to a class of medications called hormones.
It works by replacing thyroid hormone that your body is not making enough of.
Levothyroxine is used in adults and children, including newborn babies, to:
treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid - a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone).
It replaces the missing hormone whether the condition was present from birth or developed later.
It replaces the missing hormone whether the problem starts in the thyroid gland itself or in the pituitary gland or hypothalamus.
lower the level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood in people being treated for a certain type of thyroid cancer, alongside surgery and radioactive iodine therapy.
Levothyroxine injection is used in adults to treat myxedema coma.
Myxedema coma is a rare and life-threatening complication.
Myxedema coma is a complication of a severely underactive thyroid.

Immediate-release tablets:
Initial dose: 500 mg orally twice a day or 850 mg orally once a day.

Extended-release tablets:
Initial dose: 500 to 1000 mg orally once a day Dose titration: Increase in 500 mg increments weekly as tolerated Maximum dose: 2000 mg/day

Maximum dose: 2000 mg/day.

Many drugs can interact with metformin.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Not all possible interactions are listed here.
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines and any medicine you start or stop using.
Medicines that have a carbonic anhydrase inhibiting effect can raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis when taken with metformin.
Topiramate is often used for seizures or migraines.
Zonisamide is used for seizures.
Acetazolamide is used for glaucoma, altitude sickness, and other conditions.
Dichlorphenamide is used for a muscle condition called periodic paralysis.
These medicines commonly lower a substance in your blood called bicarbonate.
Your body needs bicarbonate to keep its acid levels balanced.
If you're taking metformin along with any of these medicines.
Your doctor may want to monitor you more closely.
Other medicines that may increase risk of lactic acidosis.
Some medicines can all cause metformin levels to increase.
Cimetidine is used for heartburn.

Metformin is a first-line treatment used for type 2 diabetes.

It helps improve blood sugar levels.
It is also used off-label to improve symptoms of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) and other conditions.
Metformin tablets should be used together with dietary changes and exercise for better results.

Metformin works by reducing glucose absorption from the intestines.
It works by lowering liver glucose production.
It works by improving insulin sensitivity.
Managing blood sugar levels with medications like metformin can prevent diabetes complications.
These complications include kidney damage, nerve issues, blindness, amputations, and sexual dysfunction.
Managing blood sugar levels with medications like metformin can lower the risk of cardiovascular disease.

candidates.evidence_text:
Metformin is prescribed to manage polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
It is prescribed because it improves how the body responds to insulin.
PCOS affects about 1 in 10 women of reproductive age.
PCOS is often marked by insulin resistance.
Insulin resistance is a condition in which the body doesn't respond well to insulin.
Poor response to insulin prompts the pancreas to produce more.
This excess insulin drives up androgen production.
Androgen is a male hormone.
This process worsens symptoms like irregular periods, infertility, acne, and excess hair growth.
Metformin helps by lowering insulin levels.
Metformin helps by decreasing the liver's glucose production.
Metformin helps by improving glucose uptake by muscles.
Metformin helps by reducing circulating androgen levels.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular ovulation.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular menstrual cycles.
Metformin is not FDA-approved to treat PCOS.
Metformin is widely prescribed as an off-label treatment.

candidates.evidence_text:
Common side effects:
Common side effects of metformin hydrochloride tablets include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, wind (flatulence), indigestion, and headache.
These side effects occurred in 5% or more of patients.
The patients were in the US clinical trial.
The trial was for using metformin for type 2 diabetic patients.
In the same study, 6% of patients discontinued metformin due to diarrhea.
Less common side effects were abnormal stools, hypoglycemia, myalgia, lightheadedness, dyspnea, nail disorder, rash, increased sweating, taste disorder, chest discomfort, chills, flu syndrome, flushing, and palpitation.
These side effects occurred between 1% and less than 5% of patients.
Taking your medicine with meals can help reduce these side effects.
You may find the slow-release tablets reduce gastric side effects.
Tell your doctor if the side effects bother you a lot.
Tell your doctor if the side effects last for more than a few weeks.
Tell your doctor if the side effects come back after they've gone away.
Tell your doctor if the side effects start later in therapy.

gt.entity_1: Topiramate, zonisamide, acetazolamide or dichlorphenamide combined with metformin
gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect metformin?
gt.evidence_text: Medicines that have a carbonic anhydrase inhibiting effect like topiramate (often used for seizures or migraines), zonisamide (used for seizures), acetazolamide (used for glaucoma, altitude sickness, and other conditions), and dichlorphenamide (used for a muscle condition called periodic paralysis) can raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis when taken with metformin. These medicines commonly lower a substance in your blood called bicarbonate, which your body needs to keep its acid levels balanced. If you're taking metformin along with any of these medicines, your doctor may want to monitor you more closely.

candidates.evidence_text:
Take amlodipine exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Amlodipine is usually taken once per day.
Take the medicine at the same time each day, with or without food.
Shake the oral suspension (liquid).
Measure a dose with the supplied measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Amlodipine for oral solution (Sdamlo) comes as a powder.
You must mix the powder with water.
This makes a liquid (solution) before taking or giving it.
Throw away Sdamlo if you do not take or give it within 60 minutes of mixing and get a new bottle.
Do not store mixed Sdamlo.
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
If you have high blood pressure, keep using amlodipine even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Do not change your doses or stop taking any of your medications without your doctor's advice.
Your treatment may also include diet, exercise, weight control, and blood tests.

high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or

candidates.evidence_text:
Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use this medicine if you are allergic to albuterol.
You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

candidates.subject: Albuterol Inhalation
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use this medicine if you are allergic to albuterol.
You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

candidates.evidence_text:
Losartan is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Losartan is also used to decrease the risk of stroke.
This use applies to people who have high blood pressure.
It also applies to people with a heart condition called left ventricular hypertrophy.
Left ventricular hypertrophy is the enlargement of the walls of the left side of the heart.
Losartan may not decrease the risk of stroke in African Americans who have these conditions.
Losartan is also used to treat kidney disease.
It is used in people who have type 2 diabetes.
It is used in people who have high blood pressure.
Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which the body does not use insulin normally.
Therefore, people with type 2 diabetes cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood.
Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin II receptor antagonists.
It works by blocking the action of certain natural substances.
These substances tighten the blood vessels.
Blocking them allows the blood to flow more smoothly.

candidates.subject: Losartan
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Adult Dose for Diabetic Nephropathy:
The initial dose is 50 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 100 mg orally once a day.
If hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy require titration from the initial dose, increase to 100 mg orally once a day.
If type 2 diabetic nephropathy patients require titration from the initial dose, increase to 100 mg orally once a day.
Antihypertension is substantially present within 1 week.
In some studies, the maximal effect occurred in 3 to 6 weeks.
Uses: -Treatment of hypertension.
-To reduce the risk of stroke in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy.
-Treatment of diabetic nephropathy with an elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria (urinary albumin to creatinine ratio 300 mg/g or greater) in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension.
Usual Adult Dose for Hypertension:
The initial dose is 50 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 100 mg orally once a day.

gt.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:

- heart or blood pressure medication.
- lithium.

candidates.subject: Losartan
candidates.relation_definition: Patients taking the subject drug may need the medical test or monitoring specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Take losartan exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Losartan is usually taken once per day.
You may take losartan with or without food.
Call your doctor if you are sick with vomiting or diarrhea, or if you are sweating more than usual.
You can easily become dehydrated while taking losartan.
This can lead to very low blood pressure.
This can lead to a serious electrolyte imbalance.
This can lead to kidney failure.
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
You may need frequent blood tests.
If you have high blood pressure, keep using this medicine even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture, heat, and light.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use losartan if you are allergic to it.
If you have diabetes, do not take losartan with any medication that contains aliskiren.
Aliskiren is a blood pressure medicine.
To make sure this medicine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease or congestive heart failure;
an electrolyte imbalance (such as high levels of potassium in your blood);
if you are on a low-salt diet;
liver disease; or
kidney disease.
You may also need to avoid taking losartan with aliskiren if you have kidney disease.
Stop using this medicine and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant.
Losartan can cause injury or death to the unborn baby.
You should not breastfeed while using this medicine and for 2 days after your last dose.

It works mainly on the heart.

This is why it still needs care in people with breathing problems.

Condition | Starting dose | Usual range

candidates.evidence_text:
The most common side effects of metoprolol are tiredness, dizziness, low mood (depression), diarrhea, shortness of breath, a slow heartbeat (bradycardia), and itching or rash.
Most side effects reported in studies were mild and did not last.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to metoprolol.
These signs include hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Common side effects of metoprolol:
In studies of people taking metoprolol for high blood pressure or angina:
Tiredness and dizziness occurred in about 10% of people

Metoprolol is FDA-approved to treat high blood pressure, angina, heart failure, and heart attack.
The two forms are not approved for the same conditions.
Condition | Metoprolol tartrate (immediate release) | Metoprolol succinate (extended release)
High blood pressure (hypertension) in adults | Yes | Yes
High blood pressure in children 6 years and older | No | Yes
Angina (chest pain) | Yes | Yes
Heart failure | No | Yes
Heart attack (myocardial infarction) | Yes | No
High blood pressure (hypertension).
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal heart and blood vessel events.
These events mainly include strokes and heart attacks.
Metoprolol can be used on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.
Many people need more than one medicine to reach their blood pressure goal.
Angina.
Metoprolol is used for long-term treatment of angina.
It is used to reduce how often attacks happen.
It is used to help you do more before chest pain starts.
It is not used to stop an attack that has already begun.
Heart failure.

candidates.subject: Rosuvastatin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

candidates.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

candidates.subject: major cardiovascular events
candidates.relation_definition: The subject condition or category includes the specific condition or entity specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

gt.section_title: What are the side effects of rosuvastatin?
gt.evidence_text: The most common side effects may include headache, nausea, muscle aches and pains, weakness, and constipation.

candidates.subject: Rosuvastatin
candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Common side effects:
The most common side effects may include headache, nausea, muscle aches and pains, weakness, and constipation.
Serious side effects:
Rosuvastatin may cause serious side effects, including:
Muscle pain, tenderness and weakness (myopathy).
Muscle problems, including muscle breakdown, can be serious in some people.
They rarely cause kidney damage that can lead to death.
Tell your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Tell your doctor right away if you have a fever.
Tell your doctor right away if you feel more tired than usual.
These symptoms may occur while you take this medicine.
you have muscle problems that do not go away even after your doctor has told you to stop taking this medicine.
Your doctor may do further tests to diagnose the cause of your muscle problems.
Your chances of getting muscle problems are higher if you are taking certain other medicines while you take rosuvastatin.
Your chances of getting muscle problems are higher if you are 65 years of age or older.

candidates.subject: Rosuvastatin
candidates.object: may increase risk of muscle problems
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.
Also tell the doctor who prescribes rosuvastatin if another doctor increases the dose of another medicine you are taking.
Rosuvastatin may affect the way other medicines work.
Other medicines may affect how rosuvastatin works.
Especially tell your doctor if you take:
coumarin anticoagulants (medicines that prevent blood clots, such as warfarin)
antacids (medicines you take for heartburn that contain aluminum and magnesium hydroxide)
Taking rosuvastatin with certain medicines may increase the risk of muscle problems.
Especially tell your doctor if you take:
cyclosporine (a medicine for your immune system)
teriflunomide (a medicine used to treat relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis)
enasidenib (a medicine used to treat acute myeloid leukemia)
capmatinib (a medicine for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer)
fostamatinib (a medicine used to treat low platelet counts)

gt.section_title: What are the side effects of rosuvastatin?
gt.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin may cause serious side effects, including:
- Muscle pain, tenderness and weakness (myopathy). Muscle problems, including muscle breakdown, can be serious in some people and rarely cause kidney damage that can lead to death. Tell your doctor right away if: you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially if you have a fever or feel more tired than usual, while you take this medicine. you have muscle problems that do not go away even after your doctor has told you to stop taking this medicine. Your doctor may do further tests to diagnose the cause of your muscle problems. Your chances of getting muscle problems are higher if you: are taking certain other medicines while you take rosuvastatin are 65 years of age or older are of Asian descent have thyroid problems (hypothyroidism) that are not controlled have kidney problems are taking higher doses of this medicine
- Liver problems. Your doctor may do blood tests to check your liver before you start taking this medicine and if you have symptoms of liver problems while you are taking it. Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following symptoms of liver problems: feel unusually tired or weak loss of appetite upper belly pain dark urine yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes
- Protein and blood in the urine. Rosuvastatin may cause you to have protein and blood in your urine. If you develop protein or blood in your urine, your doctor may decrease your dose.

candidates.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

fever (especially in children);
stomach pain, gas;

headache.

Omeprazole is used to treat excess stomach acid.
It is used in conditions such as stomach ulcers, heartburn, or gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
It is used in active duodenal ulcer, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and erosive esophagitis.
Omeprazole may be given together with antibiotics.
This combination is used to treat gastric ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by infection with Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori).
The treatment is for adult patients.
Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI).
Omeprazole works by blocking the acid pump in your stomach.
This reduces how much acid the stomach makes.
This gives irritated or damaged tissue a chance to heal.
Omeprazole brand names are Prilosec, Prilosec OTC.
Generic brands are available.
Omeprazole is available over the counter (OTC) and as a prescription medication.

Omeprazole works by blocking the acid pump in your stomach.
This reduces how much acid the stomach makes.
This gives irritated or damaged tissue a chance to heal.
Omeprazole brand names are Prilosec, Prilosec OTC.
Generic brands are available.
Omeprazole is available over the counter (OTC) and as a prescription medication.

candidates.subject: Gabapentin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.

Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.

Days 11 through 14: 1500 mg orally with the evening meal

The most common reason for stopping was nausea (3%).
Diarrhea (2%) was another common reason for stopping.
Agitation (2%) was also a common reason for stopping.
Insomnia (2%) was a common reason for stopping.

SSRIs including sertraline can cause sexual problems.
In men, this can mean delayed ejaculation or being unable to ejaculate.
In men, this can also mean lower sex drive.

Is sertraline the same as Zoloft?
:
Yes.
Sertraline is the active ingredient.
Zoloft is the brand name it is sold under in the United States.
Sertraline is the generic version of Zoloft.
The two contain the same medicine, sertraline hydrochloride.
You may also see it written as sertraline HCl.
Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?
:
Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.
Sertraline blocks that reabsorption.
More serotonin stays available between nerve cells.
Sertraline has very little effect on norepinephrine.
Sertraline has very little effect on dopamine.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on adrenergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on cholinergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on GABA receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on histamine receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on benzodiazepine receptors.
This lack of effect on multiple receptors is part of why sertraline is described as selective.

Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.
The most important interactions are:
MAOIs.
Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
The combination is contraindicated.
Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.
Pimozide.
Sertraline raises pimozide levels.
This can lead to QTc prolongation.
This can lead to irregular heartbeats.
The combination is contraindicated.
Other medicines that raise serotonin.
These add to the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Examples include other SSRIs and SNRIs.
Examples include triptans for migraine.
Examples include tricyclic antidepressants.
Examples include opioids.
Examples include lithium.
Examples include tryptophan.
Examples include buspirone.
Examples include amphetamines.
Examples include St. John's wort.
Blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines.
Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin, and warfarin can add to the bleeding risk.
If you take warfarin, your INR should be monitored carefully.

Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?

Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.

Breastfeeding:
Low levels of sertraline and its breakdown products pass into breast milk.
A pooled analysis of 53 mother and infant pairs was conducted.
Exclusively breastfed infants had an average of 2% of the sertraline levels measured in their mothers' blood.
The levels ranged from 0% to 15%.
No side effects were seen in those infants.
There is no information on whether sertraline affects milk production.
Talk with your doctor about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for treatment.

It is not known to be safe and effective in children under 6.
It is not known to be safe and effective for any other condition in this age group.

This monitoring is especially important early in treatment and when the dose changes.
Their weight and growth should be checked.

candidates.evidence_text:
Several medicines interact with sertraline.
Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.
The most important interactions are:
MAOIs.
Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
The combination is contraindicated.
Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.
Pimozide.
Sertraline raises pimozide levels.
This can lead to QTc prolongation.
This can lead to irregular heartbeats.
The combination is contraindicated.
Other medicines that raise serotonin.
These add to the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Examples include other SSRIs and SNRIs.
Examples include triptans for migraine.
Examples include tricyclic antidepressants.
Examples include opioids.
Examples include lithium.
Examples include tryptophan.
Examples include buspirone.
Examples include amphetamines.
Examples include St. John's wort.
Blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines.
Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin, and warfarin can add to the bleeding risk.
If you take warfarin, your INR should be monitored carefully.

candidates.evidence_text:
Is sertraline the same as Zoloft?
:
Yes.
Sertraline is the active ingredient.
Zoloft is the brand name it is sold under in the United States.
Sertraline is the generic version of Zoloft.
The two contain the same medicine, sertraline hydrochloride.
You may also see it written as sertraline HCl.
Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?
:
Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.
Sertraline blocks that reabsorption.
More serotonin stays available between nerve cells.
Sertraline has very little effect on norepinephrine.
Sertraline has very little effect on dopamine.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on adrenergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on cholinergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on GABA receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on histamine receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on benzodiazepine receptors.
This lack of effect on multiple receptors is part of why sertraline is described as selective.

What are sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules for?
:
Sertraline capsules come in 150 mg and 200 mg only.
They are not used to start treatment.
They are for people who have already been taking 100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week and need a higher dose.
The maximum is 200 mg a day, the same as for tablets.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not opened, crushed, or chewed.
If you need to come off sertraline, the dose has to be lowered gradually.
This must be done using another sertraline product.

Capsules are not approved for panic disorder.

Capsules are not approved for social anxiety disorder.
Capsules are not approved for PMDD.

:
Yes, in two ways.
Sertraline can add to warfarin's effect on bleeding risk.

candidates.evidence_text:
How long does sertraline take to work?
:
Sertraline levels in the blood become steady after about a week of once daily dosing.
The effect on symptoms takes longer.
The trials that established sertraline ran for 6 to 12 weeks.
These trials were for depression.
These trials were for OCD.
These trials were for panic disorder.
These trials were for PTSD.
These trials were for social anxiety disorder.
The trials ran for over three menstrual cycles.
These trials were for PMDD.
This duration gives a sense of the time frame over which the benefit was measured.
It takes time.
Doses are usually raised no more often than once a week.
You should keep taking sertraline even if you do not feel a change yet.
How long does sertraline stay in your system?
:
Sertraline has a half-life of about 26 hours.
This means half of what is in your blood is cleared in roughly a day.
At that rate, most of a dose has left your bloodstream within about 5 to 6 days.
Its main breakdown product, N-desmethylsertraline, lasts longer.
It has a half-life of 62 to 104 hours.
It is much less active than sertraline itself.

Eat more slowly
Eat smaller meals
Choose more bland, low-fat foods (like crackers, toast, and rice)
Avoid eating greasy, fried foods or sugar treats
Eat foods that contain water (like soup or gelatin)
Do not lie down right after eating
Drink clear or ice-cold liquids

Start Ozempic with a 0.25 mg subcutaneous injection (injection under the skin) once weekly for 4 weeks.

It is not effective for glycemic control.
After 4 weeks on the 0.25 mg dosage, increase the dosage to 0.5 mg once weekly.
If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 0.5 mg dosage.
The dosage may be increased to 1 mg once weekly.

The day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary.
The time between two doses must be at least 2 days (>48 hours).

If more than 5 days have passed, skip the missed dose.

candidates.subject: Adderall XR
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Adderall has a Boxed Warning for abuse, misuse, and addiction.
Abuse, misuse, and addiction:
Adderall has a high chance of abuse and misuse.
It may lead to substance use problems, including addiction.
Misuse and abuse of Adderall, other amphetamine-containing medicines, and methylphenidate-containing medicines can lead to overdose and death.
The risk of overdose and death is increased with higher doses.
The risk of overdose and death is increased when the medicine is used in ways that are not approved.
Examples of unapproved use include snorting or injection.
Adderall may lead to physical dependence after prolonged use, even if taken as directed.
Your healthcare provider should check you or your child for the risk of abuse, misuse, and addiction before starting treatment.
Your healthcare provider will monitor you or your child during treatment.
Tell your healthcare provider if you or your child has ever abused or been dependent on alcohol, prescription medicines, or street drugs.

candidates.evidence_text:
Take Adderall exactly as prescribed by your healthcare provider.
Follow all directions on your prescription label.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Do not take this medicine in larger or smaller amounts or for longer than recommended.
The first dose of the day is usually taken when you first wake up.
Taking this medicine in the afternoon may cause trouble sleeping.
Adderall can be taken with or without food.
Do not crush or chew an extended-release capsule.
Swallow it whole.
To make swallowing easier, you may open the capsule.
You may sprinkle the medicine into a spoonful of applesauce.
Then swallow all of the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Do not divide the medicine in the capsule.
Do not save the mixture for later use.
Adderall may be habit-forming.

Keep the medicine where others cannot get to it.

Do not take Adderall if you or your child:
are allergic to amphetamine products or any of the ingredients in Adderall (see ingredients below)
are taking, or have taken within the past 14 days, an MAO inhibitor, including the antibiotic linezolid or the intravenous medicine methylene blue.
have a rare adrenal gland tumor called pheochromocytoma.
Before taking Adderall, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions including if you or anyone in your family has ever had:
heart problems, heart disease, heart defects, or high blood pressure, or a family history of sudden death or heart problems
mental problems including psychosis, mania, bipolar illness, or depression, or a family history of suicide, bipolar illness, or depression
kidney or liver problems
seizures or an abnormal brain wave test (EEG)
circulation problems in the fingers or toes
repeated movements or sounds (tics) or Tourette's syndrome, or a family history of tics or Tourette's syndrome.
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, intending to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.

candidates.evidence_text:
Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that decreases the amount of acid produced in the stomach.
Pantoprazole is used to treat erosive esophagitis.
Erosive esophagitis is damage to the esophagus from stomach acid.
This damage is caused by gastroesophageal reflux disease, or GERD.
Pantoprazole is used in adults and children who are at least 5 years old.
Pantoprazole is usually given for up to 8 weeks at a time while your esophagus heals.
Pantoprazole is also used to treat Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other conditions involving excess stomach acid.

gt.evidence_text: Bupropion is an antidepressant medication used to treat depression and seasonal affective disorder. It also supports smoking cessation and weight management. Bupropion is the active ingredient in Wellbutrin and Zyban, Auvelity contains bupropion and dextromethorphan, and Contrave contains bupropion and naltrexone. Bupropion improves mood regulation and nicotine cravings and, when combined with naltrexone, helps reduce food intake.

candidates.evidence_text:
Examples of CYP2B6 inhibitors include ticlopidine or clopidogrel.
Bupropion inhibits CYP2D6.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antidepressants.
Examples of antidepressants include venlafaxine, nortriptyline, imipramine, desipramine, paroxetine, fluoxetine, and sertraline.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antipsychotics.
Examples of antipsychotics include haloperidol, risperidone, and thioridazine.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of beta-blockers.
An example of a beta-blocker is metoprolol.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of Type 1C antiarrhythmics.
Examples of Type 1C antiarrhythmics include propafenone and flecainide.
These medicines are metabolized by CYP2D6.
A dose reduction of these medicines may be considered when used with bupropion.
Dopaminergic drugs (levodopa and amantadine): CNS toxicity can occur when used concomitantly with this medicine.

Some people taking bupropion have severe high blood pressure.
This is especially true when using a nicotine replacement product.
The nicotine replacement product can be a patch or gum.
Your blood pressure may need to be checked before and during treatment with this medicine.
This medicine can cause you to have a false positive drug screening test (amphetamines).

For smoking cessation.
If you take bupropion to help you stop smoking, you may continue to smoke for about 1 week.
This may happen after you start the medicine.
Set a date to quit smoking during the second week of treatment.
Talk to your doctor if you are having trouble quitting after you have used bupropion for at least 7 to 12 weeks.
Your doctor may prescribe a nicotine replacement product (such as patches or gum) to help you stop smoking.
Start using the nicotine replacement product on the same day you stop (quit) smoking or using tobacco products.
You may have nicotine withdrawal symptoms when you stop smoking.

candidates.evidence_text:
You may have a higher risk of seizures if you use certain other medicines while taking bupropion.
Many drugs can interact with bupropion.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Some examples of drugs that interact with bupropion are:
Digoxin: May decrease plasma digoxin levels.
Monitor digoxin levels
MAOIs: Increased risk of hypertensive reactions can occur when used concomitantly with this medication.
Drugs that lower seizure threshold: Dose bupropion with caution.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inducers may require a dose increase if coadministered with other CYP2B6 inducers.

Dose increases should be based on clinical response.
Dose increases should not exceed the maximum recommended dose.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inhibitors may require dose adjustment if coadministered with CYP2B6 inhibitors.

candidates.evidence_text:
Examples of CYP2B6 inhibitors include ticlopidine or clopidogrel.
Bupropion inhibits CYP2D6.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antidepressants.
Examples of antidepressants include venlafaxine, nortriptyline, imipramine, desipramine, paroxetine, fluoxetine, and sertraline.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antipsychotics.
Examples of antipsychotics include haloperidol, risperidone, and thioridazine.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of beta-blockers.
An example of a beta-blocker is metoprolol.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of Type 1C antiarrhythmics.
Examples of Type 1C antiarrhythmics include propafenone and flecainide.
These medicines are metabolized by CYP2D6.
A dose reduction of these medicines may be considered when used with bupropion.
Dopaminergic drugs (levodopa and amantadine): CNS toxicity can occur when used concomitantly with this medicine.
Not all possible interactions are listed in this medication guide.

candidates.subject: Wellbutrin XL
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Do not use this medicine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
A dangerous drug interaction could occur.
MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, tranylcypromine, and others.
You should not take this medicine if you are allergic to it or if you have ever had:
a seizure disorder;
an eating disorder such as anorexia or bulimia; or
if you have suddenly stopped using alcohol, seizure medication, or a sedative (such as Xanax, Valium, Fiorinal, Klonopin, and others).
Do not take this medicine to treat more than one condition at a time.
If you take bupropion for depression, do not also take this medicine.
Do not take this medicine to quit smoking.
Do not take this medicine for weight management.
Tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions and the drugs you use.
To make sure this medicine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a head injury, seizures, or brain or spinal cord tumor;
narrow-angle glaucoma;
heart disease, high blood pressure, or a heart attack;
diabetes;

candidates.subject: Bupropion hydrobromide 174 mg oral tablet
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is related to or an alternative for the drug specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Extended-release oral tablets should be given at least 24 hours apart
Comments:
A dose of 100 mg orally four times a day may be administered.
This dose uses the 100 mg tablet.
This is done so as not to exceed the maximum single dose of 150 mg for immediate-release tablets.
Patients may be switched to the extended-release 450 mg dose.
This applies to patients taking 300 mg/day for at least 2 weeks.
This also applies to patients currently taking 450 mg/day.
These patients may be taking any formulation.
Bupropion hydrobromide 174 mg oral tablet is equivalent to bupropion hydrochloride 150 mg.
Patients should be periodically reviewed.
The review should determine the need for maintenance treatment.
The review should determine the appropriate dose for such treatment.
Usual Adult Bupropion Dose for Seasonal Affective Disorder:
Extended-release tablets:
Initial dose: 150 mg orally once a day in the morning, increased if necessary after 7 days to 300 mg orally once a day
Maintenance dose: 150 to 300 mg orally once a day
Maximum dose: 300 mg/day
Comments:

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

:
Only if your doctor tells you to.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with potassium-rich foods.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with a potassium supplement.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with a different type of diuretic.
This diuretic holds on to potassium.
Do not start any of these yourself.
Too much potassium can be harmful.
Some people on hydrochlorothiazide do not need extra potassium at all.
Is hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg enough?
:
For many people it is.
In published trials comparing the two doses, 12.5 mg kept most of the blood pressure reduction seen with 25 mg.
Low potassium was consistently less common at 12.5 mg.
Starting at 12.5 mg is recommended for adults over 65.
Your doctor will decide the right dose for you.
Your doctor may adjust it over time.

The medicine is well absorbed.
It is not broken down by the body.
It is cleared by the kidneys.
Most of a dose passes out unchanged in the urine.

Its half-life means the time for blood levels to fall by half.
In people with kidney disease, levels in the blood are higher.
In people with kidney disease, the medicine stays in the body longer.
Hydrochlorothiazide controls high blood pressure but does not cure it.
Keep taking it even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often causes no symptoms.

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

gt.evidence_text: Hydrochlorothiazide works by inhibiting the kidneys from reabsorbing sodium and chloride, so more salt and water leave the body in the urine, which helps reduce excess fluid buildup (edema). Exactly how thiazides lower blood pressure is not fully understood. The early effect is thought to come from a drop in blood volume. With longer-term use, blood volume returns towards normal while the blood vessels themselves offer less resistance to blood flow. Hydrochlorothiazide does not usually change blood pressure that is already normal.

Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.
It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures
Kidney and liver problems:
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject entity raises the quantity or amount of the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Fluid and salt imbalance:
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.
It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures
Kidney and liver problems:
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are unable to pass urine (anuria).
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are allergic to hydrochlorothiazide or to other sulfonamide-derived medicines (sometimes called sulfa drugs).
Before you start HCTZ, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels
high cholesterol or high triglycerides
high calcium levels or a parathyroid gland disorder
low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma
an allergy to sulfa medicines or to penicillin
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause jaundice or bleeding problems in a newborn.
The medicine can pass into breast milk.
The medicine may cause serious side effects in a nursing baby.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will take this medicine.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will breastfeed.

The medicine is well absorbed.
It is not broken down by the body.
It is cleared by the kidneys.

Its half-life means the time for blood levels to fall by half.
In people with kidney disease, levels in the blood are higher.
In people with kidney disease, the medicine stays in the body longer.
Hydrochlorothiazide controls high blood pressure but does not cure it.
Keep taking it even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often causes no symptoms.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.object: increasing the amount of urine the body makes
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.

It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures

HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines

40mg of fluoxetine is considered a moderate maintenance dose in adults for major depressive disorder (MDD) and OCD.
The standard starting dose for most conditions is 20mg per day.
The starting dose for panic disorder is 10mg.
If symptoms have not improved after several weeks, the dose may be increased.

The recommended dose for bulimia is 60mg per day.
Your doctor will determine the right dose for you based on your condition and response to treatment.
Does fluoxetine cause weight gain?
:
Fluoxetine is less likely to cause weight gain than many other antidepressants.
In the short term, it can actually cause mild weight loss.
This is due to reduced appetite.
Reduced appetite is one of its common side effects.
However, some people do experience weight changes over longer-term use.
If you notice significant weight changes while taking this medicine, speak to your doctor.
Dose adjustments or alternative treatments may be available.

candidates.evidence_text:
How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

candidates.evidence_text:
Is 40mg of fluoxetine a high dose?
40mg of fluoxetine is considered a moderate maintenance dose in adults for major depressive disorder (MDD) and OCD.
The standard starting dose for most conditions is 20mg per day.
The starting dose for panic disorder is 10mg.
If symptoms have not improved after several weeks, the dose may be increased.
The dose may be increased up to 40mg for MDD and OCD.
The dose may be increased up to 20mg for panic disorder.
The recommended dose for bulimia is 60mg per day.
Your doctor will determine the right dose for you based on your condition and response to treatment.
Does fluoxetine cause weight gain?
:
Fluoxetine is less likely to cause weight gain than many other antidepressants.
In the short term, it can actually cause mild weight loss.
This is due to reduced appetite.
Reduced appetite is one of its common side effects.
However, some people do experience weight changes over longer-term use.
If you notice significant weight changes while taking this medicine, speak to your doctor.
Dose adjustments or alternative treatments may be available.

Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps regulate mood, emotions, and sleep. By increasing the availability of serotonin, fluoxetine can relieve symptoms of depression, anxiety, and OCD.

Fluoxetine works by blocking the reabsorption of serotonin in the brain.
This process leaves more serotonin active between nerve cells.
The reabsorption of serotonin is also known as reuptake.
Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps regulate mood, emotions, and sleep.
Fluoxetine can relieve symptoms of depression, anxiety, and OCD.
Fluoxetine relieves these symptoms by increasing the availability of serotonin.
Fluoxetine belongs to a class of antidepressants called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).
SSRIs are one of the most commonly prescribed antidepressant classes.
They are generally well-tolerated.
They are effective across a range of conditions.

How long does fluoxetine stay in your system?
:
Fluoxetine stays in your system longer than most other antidepressants.
After stopping this medicine, it takes approximately 1 to 4 days for the drug itself to be reduced by half.
Fluoxetine converts in the body to an active metabolite called norfluoxetine.
Norfluoxetine has a much longer half-life of 4 to 16 days.
This means this medicine and its active metabolite can remain detectable in your system.
They can remain detectable for up to 5 weeks.
This duration is after your last dose.
This is clinically important for two reasons:
Switching medications requires a washout period.
This applies if you are switching from fluoxetine to certain other antidepressants.
These other antidepressants include MAOIs.
Your doctor will require a washout period of at least 5 weeks.
This period allows fluoxetine to fully clear your system.
This avoids dangerous drug interactions.
Stopping fluoxetine.

gt.section_title: Who Should Not Take This Medicine?
gt.evidence_text:
Do not take fluoxetine if you:
- Are allergic to fluoxetine or any of its ingredients
- Currently take a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), including the antibiotic linezolid. If you are unsure whether your medication is an MAOI, ask your doctor or pharmacist
- Stopped taking an MAOI in the last 2 weeks
- Currently take pimozide (Orap) as this combination can cause a serious, potentially life-threatening irregular heart rhythm
- Currently taking thioridazine (Mellaril) as this combination can cause a dangerous irregular heart rhythm

candidates.subject: Fluoxetine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used together with the other treatment or lifestyle measure specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Fluoxetine is FDA-approved to treat the following conditions:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 8 years and older
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 7 years and older
Bulimia nervosa for acute and maintenance treatment of binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia
Panic disorder for the treatment of panic attacks in adults
When used in combination with olanzapine, fluoxetine is also FDA-approved for:
Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older
Treatment-resistant depression for adults who have not responded to at least two adequate antidepressant trials
Fluoxetine alone is not approved for bipolar I depressive episodes or treatment-resistant depression.
Olanzapine must be used in combination for these indications.

candidates.subject: Fluoxetine

candidates.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions.
Tell your doctor about all your medications.
Do this before starting fluoxetine (Prozac).
Some medical conditions may interact with fluoxetine.
Some medications may interact with fluoxetine.
Some conditions or medications may affect whether fluoxetine is safe for you.
Tell your doctor if you take any of the following medications or supplements:
Triptans (for migraine)
Antidepressants or mood stabilizers, including SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, MAOIs, lithium, buspirone, or antipsychotics
Amphetamines
Opioid pain medications, including tramadol, fentanyl, meperidine, or methadone
Over-the-counter supplements such as St. John's Wort or tryptophan
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
Many of these combinations can increase the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Serotonin syndrome is a potentially serious condition.
Tell your doctor if you have or have had any of the following:
Liver, kidney, or heart problems
Seizures or epilepsy
Bipolar disorder or mania
Low sodium levels in the blood
A stroke or high blood pressure
Bleeding problems
Pregnancy

Initial dose: 150 mg orally per day in divided doses; this may be increased by 50 mg orally per day every 3 to 4 days Maximum dose: -Inpatients: 600 mg/day -Outpatients: 400 mg/day Comments: -Patients should be screened for a personal/family history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania prior to initiating treatment. -Patients should be monitored for withdrawal symptoms when discontinuing therapy. -After an adequate response has been reached, dosage may be gradually reduced depending on therapeutic response. -If drowsiness develops, a major portion of the daily dose may be administered at bedtime or a reduction of dosage may be necessary. -This drug should be taken shortly after a meal or light snack. Use: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD)

candidates.evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.

This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.

Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.
