candidates.evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Tell your doctor if you have any type of allergy.

candidates.subject: Flonase Nasal Spray
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidates.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidates.evidence_text:
Before using Flonase Nasal Spray, tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or cataracts.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, diabetes, herpes simplex virus of your eyes, tuberculosis, or any other infection.
Tell your doctor if you have sores or ulcers inside your nose.
Tell your doctor if you have recently had injury of or surgery on your nose.
You may start to feel relief on the first day.
It can take several days of regular once-daily use before you get the full effect.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 7 days.
Tell your doctor if you develop new symptoms such as severe facial pain or thick nasal discharge.
Corticosteroids can affect the way your immune system responds to infection.
Avoid being near people who are sick or have infections.
Stop use and ask a doctor if you have, or come into contact with someone who has, chickenpox, measles, or tuberculosis.
Do not administer Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray to a child younger than 4 years old.
Do not administer Flonase Sensimist to a child younger than 2 years.

gt.evidence_text: Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH. These symptoms include a weak urine stream, trouble starting to urinate, dribbling, a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely, needing to urinate often or urgently, and getting up at night to urinate.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

They include dribbling.

Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

Take once a day, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day.

Swallow the capsule whole.
Do not crush, chew, break, or open it.

Usual adult dose for benign prostatic hyperplasia:
0.4 mg by mouth once a day, taken about half an hour after the same meal each day.
If symptoms have not improved after 2 to 4 weeks at 0.4 mg.

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg should not be taken with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
If tamsulosin is stopped or interrupted for several days.
Treatment should start again.
The treatment should start at 0.4 mg once a day.

What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is not indicated or used to treat or manage the condition or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:

a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:

headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.

candidates.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, itching, rash, swelling of your face, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing.
Rarely, tamsulosin has been linked to severe skin reactions with blistering and peeling of the skin.
Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:
a lightheaded feeling, like you might pass out
a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin

moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

Apixaban can cause a serious blood clot.
This can happen if you undergo a procedure.
The procedure could be a spinal tap.
The procedure could be receiving spinal anesthesia.

This type of blood clot could cause permanent or long-term paralysis.
Apixaban can make it easier for you to bleed, even from a minor injury.
Call your doctor if you have any bleeding that will not stop.

artificial heart valve;
a history of problems with your spine, a spinal surgery, or difficult or repeated spinal taps;
bleeding problems;
plan for surgery, or a medical or a dental procedure;
a thin tube (catheter) placed in your back to give you certain medicine;
antiphospholipid syndrome, an immune system disorder that increases the risk of blood clots; or
liver or kidney disease.
It is not known if apixaban will harm an unborn baby.
Taking apixaban during pregnancy may cause bleeding in the mother or the unborn baby.
